# Deliver a user's conversation list over the WebSocket protocol

Issue: re-cinq/HALEngine#144
Labels: type:feature, size:M, area:api, area:compliance, epic:extension-points

Part of #35

## Why

#143 gives a consumer `store.listFor(userId)`.
It does not give a **client** anything: the browser holding the socket cannot reach the store, so
every consumer that wants a history sidebar has to stand up its own authenticated HTTP route over
the same data the engine already authenticated on the upgrade. That is a second authorisation
path to the same personal data, written once per consumer, each one able to get the ownership
check wrong in its own way — the exact failure #45 went out of its way to avoid for resume.

A consumer may have no such route to extend: an engine deployment behind an api with a session
store and no conversation endpoints of its own has nothing to add this to. The engine already knows who is connected and already
replays a conversation on resume; answering "which conversations do I have" over the same socket
is the smaller surface.

## What to do

- `src/types/messages.ts`, additive only:
  - `ListConversationsMessage {type: 'list_conversations'; limit?: number; before?: string}` into
    `IncomingMessage`. There is no user id field, and that is the point: the list is always the
    connection's authenticated user's.
  - `ConversationListMessage {type: 'conversation_list'; conversations: ConversationSummary[]}`
    into `OutgoingMessage`, where `ConversationSummary` is `SessionSummary` with its two times as
    ISO strings — `Date` does not survive `JSON.stringify` as a `Date`, and the protocol types
    describe what goes on the wire.
- `validation.ts`: a `list_conversations` case — `limit`, when present, an integer 1–200;
  `before`, when present, a string `Date.parse` accepts. Anything else is `INVALID_MESSAGE`, as
  the two existing cases do it.
- Handling: `createMessageHandler` takes the session store and the new options alongside the
  orchestrator (`createServer` already holds both), and answers `list_conversations` on the
  non-locked path beside `ping` — a history request is not a turn and must not queue behind a
  streaming answer.
- The user id comes from `ws.userId`, never from the frame. Add the regression:
  a frame carrying an extra `userId` of another user is answered with the connecting user's own
  list.
- Opt-in: `HalEngineConfig.transport.history?: {enabled: boolean}`, default off, threaded through
  `createServer`'s options like `resume`. With it off, `list_conversations` is answered with an
  `error` frame and no list.
- A store that implements no `listFor` is answered with an `error`, not an empty list: a client
  that renders "no conversations" for a user who has several is a worse answer than one that
  renders a failure. `ErrorCodes` gains one code for both cases (`UNSUPPORTED`), additive.
- Picking a conversation needs nothing new: the client reconnects with `?sessionId=<id>`, which
  #45 already ships with the ownership check and the replay. No in-band switch frame, no second
  replay path.
- Specs and docs: extend `specs/hal-engine-websocket-protocol/spec.md` (the two frames, their
  field tables, the authorisation rule) and the conversation-list spec; add § Conversation list
  to `docs/getting-started.md` by editing `example/full-config.ts` and running `npm run docs:fix`
  — that listing sits under `<!-- doc-block: example/full-config.ts#full-config -->` and
  `npm run docs:check` fails a hand-edited block.

## Decisions

- **A frame, not a REST route.** The REST chat routes are demo-only and are not where a consumer is meant to build. The WebSocket is where the caller is
  already authenticated, once per connection, by the consumer's own `wsAuth`.
- **Its own opt-in flag, separate from `resume`.** Resume hands a client back a conversation it
  was already in; a list tells it what else the user has. A deployer who turned on resume did not
  thereby agree to the second disclosure, and a config that conflates them cannot be audited.
- **Answered off the per-session lock.** `PerSessionLock` serialises turns (#47). A list request
  that queued behind a two-minute streaming answer would look broken, and it mutates nothing.
- **An error, not an empty list, when it cannot be answered.** See above; silence that looks like
  data is the one failure mode a history view cannot recover from.
- **Answered when asked, never pushed.** No `conversation_list` arrives unsolicited: a client
  that just started a conversation knows, and a push would need a fan-out across the sockets a
  resumed session can be open on.
- **The frame is accepted by `validateMessage` whether or not the feature is on**, and the
  handler is what refuses it. Validation is static and has no config; the alternative is
  threading options into a pure validator to turn a type into "unknown".

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/types/messages.ts` gains only new interfaces and their two union members (**amended:** four interfaces, not two — each frame needs a type for its own payload, `ConversationCursor` for what a client sends back and `ConversationSummary` for a row on the wire) — a
      `git diff` of that file touches no existing line, and a fixture pins that every message
      literal valid before this change still compiles
- [ ] `validateMessage({type: 'list_conversations'})` is valid; with `limit: 0`, `limit: 201`,
      `limit: 1.5`, `limit: '10'` or `before: 'not a date'` it is invalid with a message naming
      the field
- [ ] With `history: {enabled: true}` and a store holding three conversations for the user, a
      `list_conversations` frame is answered with exactly one `conversation_list` carrying three
      summaries, newest first, each `createdAt` and `updatedAt` an ISO string, and no
      `stream_end`
- [ ] A frame carrying `{type: 'list_conversations', userId: '<another user>'}` is answered with
      the connecting user's own list, and the store's `listFor` is called with `ws.userId` —
      asserted on the recorded argument, not only on the frame
- [ ] `limit` and `before` reach `listFor` as the frame sent them. **Amended:** `before` is a
      `{updatedAt, sessionId}` cursor of ISO strings, not a `Date`. This was written before
      #143's review found that paging on a timestamp alone drops a conversation whenever two
      share an activity time, so the store's cursor became a composite that accepts an ISO
      string; a `Date` cannot carry the tie-break. The handler passes `{limit, before}` with
      both possibly `undefined` rather than omitting the argument, which is the same call
- [ ] With `history` absent, the same frame is answered with one `error` frame whose code is
      `UNSUPPORTED` and no `conversation_list`
- [ ] With `history: {enabled: true}` against a store implementing no `listFor`, the answer is
      the same `error` frame, and `grep` shows no code path that sends `conversations: []`
- [ ] A `listFor` that rejects is answered with one `error` frame whose code is `SERVER_ERROR`
      and whose message carries no store detail, the socket stays open, and the failure is
      logged with the session id and no user content. **Added during the build:** a store throwing
      the new exported `StoreCannotList` is answered `UNSUPPORTED` instead, so an injected
      collection without a `find` reads as the misconfiguration it is rather than a database
      that failed
- [ ] A `list_conversations` sent while a `user_message` is streaming on the same session is
      answered before that turn's `stream_end` — it does not wait on the lock
- [ ] A client that takes an id from a `conversation_list` and reconnects with `?sessionId=<id>`
      receives `resumed: true` and that conversation's replay, with no new transport code: the
      test exercises the existing #45 path end to end
- [ ] `ConnectedMessage` is unchanged by this issue
- [ ] **GDPR.** The protocol spec states that `conversation_list` carries one authenticated
      user's own conversation metadata and no conversation content, that the user id is taken
      from the connection and never from the frame, and that `transport.history` is the
      deployer's decision to make a user's history reachable from the client; `SessionResumeOptions`'
      retention note is mirrored on the new options type, pointing at #41
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` carries an entry under `## [Unreleased]` written for somebody installing the
      package
- [ ] The `docs/getting-started.md` change is made in `example/full-config.ts` and the doc
      regenerated with `npm run docs:fix`, not typed into the markdown
- [ ] Spec statements carry trailing `([validated by: ...](...#Lnn))` citations, `Status` rows
      match coverage, and `npm run check:spec-links`, `npm run check:spec-status` and
      `npm run spec:names` pass
- [ ] The version bump is MINOR — new optional config, two additive protocol frames, one new
      error code — and the PR body says so; no migration guide is owed
- [ ] `npm run verify` passes and the coverage floors for the touched groups hold or rise

## Amendments

Three things changed between writing this issue and building it, each marked in the criterion it
affects:

1. **`before` is a cursor, not a timestamp.** #143's review found that paging on `updatedAt` alone
   silently drops a conversation when two share an activity time. The store's cursor became
   `{updatedAt, sessionId}`, so the frame carries both halves and the validator refuses one half
   alone. Built as originally written, the transport would have reintroduced the defect the store
   had just been fixed for.
2. **`messages.ts` gains four interfaces, not two** — the two frames plus the two payload types
   they describe.
3. **`StoreCannotList` is new public surface**, beyond what this issue specified: without it a
   permanent store misconfiguration cannot be told from a transient failure, in either the client
   frame or the log.

Two decisions the criteria did not anticipate:

- **`transport.history` without `transport.resume` is useless, and now says so.** `?sessionId=` is
  read only when resume is enabled, so a list whose rows cannot be opened is a deployment slip:
  the engine warns at startup and the documentation says so where it tells a client to reconnect
  with a row's id. Refusing to start was considered and rejected as too blunt for a library.
- **The conversation the connection is in is listed like any other**, so a fresh connect sees a row
  of its own holding no entries. Filtering it out was rejected: it is a real conversation the user
  is in, and it is their newest the moment they send anything.

## Tech notes

Depends on #143: without `listFor` there is
nothing to send.

Key paths: `src/types/messages.ts`, `src/types/session.ts` (`ErrorCodes`),
`src/transport/ws/{validation,messageHandler,sender}.ts`, `src/transport/createServer.ts`,
`src/config.ts`, `example/full-config.ts`, `specs/hal-engine-websocket-protocol/spec.md`.

Out of scope: a preview or title on the summaries (its own issue); deleting a conversation from
the client, which would put an erasure primitive on the wire and needs its own authorisation
decision; paging state held server-side — the client pages with `before`; an operator view of
another user's conversations, which is an authorisation question of its own; and live sync between open tabs,
which #124 ruled out.

Refs #143, #145, #41, #45, #47, #124

specs/hal-engine-session-resume/spec.md:- Resume is the optional `transport.resume` config, off by default; without it, a reconnect naming an earlier id gets a new id, a `connected` frame with exactly its four original fields, and no replay ([validated by: with resume absent, answers a reconnect naming the first id with a new id and no replay](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L180)).
specs/hal-engine-session-resume/spec.md:- With resume off, a socket opened at `{basePath}/ws/undefined` still completes the handshake and gets a server-minted id ([validated by: with resume off, still completes a handshake at /hal/ws/undefined and mints an id](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L412)).
specs/hal-engine-session-resume/spec.md:- The owner reconnecting with the id from their first `connected` frame receives `resumed: true` and `entryCount` equal to the stored entries, followed by one `entry_upsert` per entry at its own index, equal to what is stored ([validated by: with resume on, answers the owner reconnecting with resumed true, entryCount 2 and both stored entries](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L196)).
specs/hal-engine-session-resume/spec.md:- A resumed session takes the credentials of the socket that resumed it, and the socket it replaced closing afterwards leaves them alone, though that close still calls `onDisconnect`, since the hooks are per connection ([validated by: keeps the credentials of the socket that resumed a session when the socket it replaced closes](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L262)).
specs/hal-engine-session-resume/spec.md:- A session open on more than one socket carries the credentials of the newest; when that socket closes, it takes those of the newest one still open, so a tab left open keeps working, and they are cleared only when the last one closes ([validated by: gives a session back the credentials of a socket still open when the socket that resumed it closes](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L281)).
specs/hal-engine-session-resume/spec.md:- `onConnect` receives `{resumed}` as its second argument: `false` for the connection that started a session and `true` for each one that resumed it ([validated by: tells onConnect whether a connection started its session or resumed it](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L301)).
specs/hal-engine-session-resume/spec.md:- An entry still streaming when its session is resumed, because its turn is running on the socket that started it, is replayed with `isStreaming: false` and `truncated: true`, since its deltas and commit go to that socket and a client shown it streaming would wait for a commit that never comes, while the stored entry stays as the running turn leaves it ([validated by: replays an entry whose turn is still running as finished and truncated, leaving the stored entry as it is](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L364)).
specs/hal-engine-session-resume/spec.md:- A stored entry a tool suppressed is replayed as `entry_skip`, so the client sees the conversation it saw live and never the text a tool hid ([validated by: replays a suppressed entry as a skip, so the client never sees text a tool suppressed](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L328)).
specs/hal-engine-session-resume/spec.md:- An answer still open when suppression begins is first committed as streamed so far, then retracted and marked like any sent answer, and the text after it opens a new entry the client is only sent as a skip, so a replay leaves the client as blank as the live stream did ([validated by: commits and retracts an answer still open when suppression begins, and skips what follows as a new entry](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L267), [validated by: replays an answer suppressed while it was still open as skips, as blank as the live client was left](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L351)).
specs/hal-engine-session-resume/spec.md:- An id is resumed only for the stored session's own user: another user naming it receives a fresh session, `resumed: false` and `resumeFailure: 'unknown'`, with frames identical to the response for an id that was never issued, so the answer cannot be used to learn which ids exist ([validated by: answers another user naming the id exactly as it answers an id that was never issued](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L213)).
specs/hal-engine-session-resume/spec.md:- An id that was never issued receives `resumed: false` with `resumeFailure: 'unknown'`, no replay and no `error` frame ([validated by: answers a never-issued id with resumed false, resumeFailure unknown, and no replay or error](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L227)).
specs/hal-engine-session-resume/spec.md:- A requested id is never adopted as the key of a new session, which would be session fixation: the store then holds one session, under the id the server minted ([validated by: never adopts a requested id as a key: one session, under the id the server minted](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L240)).
specs/hal-engine-session-resume/spec.md:- Whether an id is resumable is the store's `get` answer: an id it returns a session for is resumed, and one it returns nothing for starts fresh ([validated by: resumes the id its store knows and starts fresh for one it does not](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L313)).
specs/hal-engine-session-resume/spec.md:- A resumed session whose socket closes before its replay is kept, never evicted: eviction erases, and it is reserved for a new session no client ever received ([validated by: keeps a resumed session whose socket closed before the replay, rather than evicting it](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L378)).
specs/hal-engine-session-resume/spec.md:- A socket closing under resume still calls `onDisconnect` with its session id ([validated by: still calls onDisconnect with the session id when a socket closes under resume](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L253)).
specs/hal-engine-session-resume/spec.md:- With `latest` on, a connect that names no `?sessionId=` rejoins the user's most recently active session, which the store's optional `latestFor(userId)` returns, with the same `resumed: true`, `entryCount`, replay and `onConnect` `{resumed: true}` as a named resume ([validated by: with latest on, rejoins the most recently active session of a user whose connect names none](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L428)).
specs/hal-engine-session-resume/spec.md:- It starts a new session for a user who has none, and for a connect that sends `?new=1`, which is how a client starts a new conversation on purpose while a latest one exists ([validated by: with latest on, starts a new session for a user with none, and on ?new=1 even when one exists](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L445)).
specs/hal-engine-session-resume/spec.md:- A connect that names an id rejoins that session, whichever is latest ([validated by: with latest on, still rejoins the session a connect names rather than the latest one](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L460)).
specs/hal-engine-session-resume/spec.md:- A session `latestFor` answers for another user is never rejoined, and a `latestFor` that throws or that the store does not implement starts a new session ([validated by: starts a new session when the store's latestFor answers another user's session, throws, or is absent](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L472)).
specs/hal-engine-session-resume/spec.md:- Without `latest`, a connect that names no id starts a new session, as before ([validated by: with resume on but latest off, starts a new session for a connect that names none](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L496)).
specs/hal-engine-session-resume/spec.md:- A connect naming its own session after it aged out gets `resumed: false`, `resumeFailure: 'expired'`, a new `sessionId` and no replay ([validated by: tells the owner of a session that aged out that it expired, with a new id and no replay](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L519)).
specs/hal-engine-session-resume/spec.md:- Another user naming that expired id gets `resumeFailure: 'unknown'`, in a response identical to the one for an id never issued, so `expired` reveals nothing about an id that is not the caller's ([validated by: answers another user naming an expired id exactly as it answers an id never issued](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L535)).
specs/hal-engine-session-resume/spec.md:- A connect that names no id gets no `resumeFailure` at all, even when the latest-session default finds nothing to rejoin ([validated by: sends no resumeFailure at all when the connect names no id, even with no latest session to rejoin](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L548)).
specs/hal-engine-session-resume/spec.md:- Resume reads a named id with one call per attempt, the store's `lookup` when it has one and its `get` otherwise, and either way resumes a live session and answers a dead id `unknown` ([validated by: reads a named id with one call per attempt: lookup when the store has it, get otherwise](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L559)).
specs/hal-engine-session-resume/spec.md:- `ConnectedMessage` gains only the optional `resumed`, `entryCount` and `resumeFailure`, so a `connected` literal carrying neither still type-checks ([validated by: still types a connected frame literal that carries neither resume field](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L420)).
specs/hal-engine-websocket-protocol/spec.md:- An entry still streaming when its conversation is resumed is replayed with `isStreaming: false` and `truncated: true`: the rest of its turn streams to the connection that started it, so this one would wait for a commit that never comes ([validated by: replays an entry whose turn is still running as finished and truncated, leaving the stored entry as it is](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L364)).
specs/hal-engine-websocket-protocol/spec.md:- With the server's `latest` option, a client that has lost the id, after a page refresh for instance, MAY connect without one and still rejoin its user's most recent conversation, and sends `?new=1` to start a new conversation instead ([validated by: with latest on, rejoins the most recently active session of a user whose connect names none](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L428), [validated by: with latest on, starts a new session for a user with none, and on ?new=1 even when one exists](../../src/transport/sessionResume.test.ts#L445)).
